findings.title: Full-size badge covers the gizmo's own label when it wraps to two lines
findings.detail: Command.GizmoOnGUIInt draws LabelCap at Rect(butRect.x, butRect.yMax - num + 12f, width, num) on GrayTextBG. A two-line Tiny label starts about yMax-18, which is exactly the badge rect (button.yMax - size.y - 2f). The badge is drawn after, in the Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI postfix, so it hides the start of the label. Multi-select pawnLabel 'Ability (Name)' (Command_Ability.cs:81) is the likeliest to wrap. Even one-line labels overlap the badge by about 2px. In Badge, for full-size buttons only, measure labelH = Text.CalcHeight(command.LabelCap, button.width + 0.1f) under GameFont.Tiny and put the badge's bottom at button.yMax - labelH + 12f - 1f. Badge needs a 'shrunk' parameter, because shrunk buttons draw no label.

findings.title: Shrunk badge only just fits: 'auto+' fills about 35 of 36 px
findings.detail: Command.GetShrunkSize is 36f. The badge rect is x+3 with width size.x+4, so any translation of AAI_Badge_Full/AAI_Badge_Stationary longer than about 29px at Tiny font spills past the button's right edge onto the next shrunk gizmo. Vertically it clears the shrunk hotkey at (3,0). Clamping r.width to button.width - 6f would keep translations inside the button.

findings.title: Badge keeps full colour on a greyed-out (disabled or low-light) gizmo
findings.detail: Vanilla tints labels with LowLightLabelColor when parms.lowLight is set. The badge always uses BadgeColor, so on an ability that is cooling down or disabled it stands out against the grey. This is a cosmetic opinion, not a collision.
